references.text: The parallel text in Exodus containing the fourth commandment about the Sabbath, with the same instruction to work for six days.
Reiterates the principle of six days of work followed by rest, in the context of the sabbatical year and the weekly Sabbath.
Confirms the pattern of six working days as part of the Sabbath command given to Moses.
Repeats the instruction to work for six days, even during plowing and harvest seasons.
Refers to the six working days in connection with the holiness of the Sabbath.
Ezekiel mentions the six working days in contrast to the Sabbath in his vision of the future temple.
The synagogue leader refers to the six working days when he criticizes healing on the Sabbath.
